schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The first real device on the spine — the system's notary and its proving mechanism (MAP.md:569). `TesterDevice` subclasses `BaseDevice` (so it carries CP1-CP6 and reports the Form v0 #2 surface). Its capabilities today: (1) `run_proof(path)` — run a proof file as a subprocess and PRODUCE a VALIDATION record (the ratified eight fields: claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon); the verdict is read from the subject's exit code, not granted. (2) It OWNS THE NETWORK (MAP.md:333): `run_proof(..., isolation='netns')` runs the subject inside a MEASURED network seal (`cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py`) — the seal is probed from inside (never assumed) and its verdict is folded into the record's `method`+`evidence`, no ninth field. An unconfirmable seal is INDETERMINATE (CP1) and never launders into a green.
why: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass; the verdict must come from a hand the builder did not guide. Placing that gate in a device (not a convention each builder self-applies) is Law 4 (physics over policy): the proving and the attesting come from the same hand, so a green cannot be self-granted. This is the smallest honest version of the tester — it proves, it attests, it dogfoods (its first act validates the real base proofs) — while the pillars it will grow (network ownership, a durable store, richer verdict methods) stay filed edges, built when a real need pulls them (round-three discipline: simplest provable stone first).

feedback.why: A SELF-ROUTE, AND IT IS THE MEASURED ANSWER RATHER THAN A FALLBACK. inspect_trail's lanes are about the validation trail's own integrity — an entry that is not a VALIDATION record, a record with no trail_link, a link that does not match the chain. persist_validation is THE ONLY HAND THAT MINTS A LINK (validation_store.py:303, and the door refuses a caller-supplied one at :447), and that hand lives at this address. Akien's rule for the -2- edge, 2026-08-14, verbatim: "the purpose of an inspector/gate combination is to qa THE OUTPUT OF THE THING BEFORE IT THATS COMING IN AS ITS INPUT. IF IT FAILS, GENERALLY THAT FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE UPSTREAM CREATIVE ENTITY. In some cases it skips levels." REFINED BY HIM THE SAME DAY, and the refinement is what `to` MEANS: "really it shouldn't be 'number of steps' it should be 'to the feedback target' which is likely to be the previous step." So this field is not a hop count and never was — it names the TARGET. The previous step is the common case, not the definition, and a route that lands elsewhere is not a special case needing a count. Here there is no upstream party: nothing outside this device can author a well-formed trail record, so a trail defect can only have come from this door or from something that wrote past it. Routing it anywhere else would be delivering feedback to a party structurally unable to act on it, which is the failure mode a plausible default destination produces and the reason NoRoute refuses rather than defaults.

invoke: command line: `cairn test [paths...] [--netns] [--timeout N] [-q]` — the registered address for running proofs (bin/cmd/test -> cairn/devices/tester/cli.py). No argument runs every proof in the repo; a directory expands beneath it. import: `from cairn.devices.tester.device import TesterDevice`. Prove: `cairn test cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_cli.py` (exit 0 = green).

the_verb.why_it_exists: Measured 2026-07-30: a session spent four tool calls answering 'how do I run a proof here?' — and its FIRST guess was `cairn test`, the right address, which was empty. The answer existed, in each proof's docstring, which you can only read once you have already found the file. A docstring is not an address (Law 1: compiling an answer means putting it where the question is ASKED, not where the answer is true). The dispatcher already fails loud and lists its own verbs, so registering `test` turns four calls into one, permanently.
the_verb.routes_through_the_real_door: Every run goes through TesterDevice.run_proof — same notary, same isolation machinery, same exit-code-is-the-verdict rule as the sealing chokepoint. A convenience runner shelling out to `python3 <proof>` would have been faster to write and would LIE: green there would not mean green at the door, and the divergence surfaces under time pressure. This system has already paid that bill once (the netns sealing, 2026-07-29).
the_verb.seals_nothing: run_proof returns the eight fields and persists none of them; the standing-lesson gate is the write-door. This verb keeps that split and writes no record at all — a dev command typed twenty times an hour must not mint entries in a record of truth. That IS the diagnostic-surface / record-of-truth line Law 7 turns on, and proofs/test_cli.py pins it by asserting the run leaves no new file beside the proof it ran.
the_verb.cannot_go_green_over_nothing: A typo'd path is loud and exits non-zero. A runner that matched zero proofs and exited 0 would report success in the exact shape of real success — the most expensive lie available to it, because nobody investigates a green (Law 8).
the_verb.a_red_is_complete_on_the_first_run: The failing proof's stdout and stderr tails and its exit code print immediately. A diagnostic that forces a re-run to find out why has failed at its job, and re-running to gather what the first report should have carried is re-derivation.

node_class: device — the first runtime component on the spine (base/ is the code-seam it stands on).
entry: FRESH design, MECHANISM grafted. The tester's design — device-hood, the VALIDATION record, the seal's four verdicts mapped to CP1/Law 3, the seal recorded INSIDE the VALIDATION rather than a parallel record — is Cairn's, authored to Form v0 (like device.py/shim.py). The seal's OS PLUMBING crosses nearly literally from UU's isolation.py (the `bwrap --unshare-net --cap-add CAP_NET_ADMIN` flag string, the inside-probe, the `available()` apparmor check) because it is kernel truth, not a design Cairn replaced. What did NOT cross: UU's netpolicy Router (fixture/refuse/forward + the nftables reject+counter) — the programmable-network pillar, deferred (see open edge (b)); and UU's verdict shape (seal_confirmed/seal_detail/duration_s), replaced by the Cairn VALIDATION.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why, the operational voyage lives in the sidecars (Law 1/4/7)
filed_edges: (b) the seal delivers NO ROUTE (the closed half); the CHOSEN ROUTE — a Router that serves a FIXTURE, REFUSES with a kernel counter, or FORWARDS over a Unix socket — is deferred, pulled by db_domain (FORWARD to Postgres) and inference_domain (FIXTURE/REFUSE); it advances but does NOT retire CLAUDE.md's 'reached only through the domain' IOUs
(c) the verdict METHOD is exit-code + seal only — quorum / review-by-N-experts for concept pieces (MAP.md:752) is a later method the `method` field names room for
(d) reported-vs-filed intention drift detection is not wired
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_tester.py, runnable bare (python3) today; the tester will eventually own how proofs run, including its own. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed.
falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) `run_proof` on a passing proof yields anything but green, or on a failing proof anything but red (the notary must not lie); (2) a VALIDATION record's field-set is not exactly the ratified eight (drift — extra or missing field), including when the seal rides inside it; (3) `TesterDevice` stops subclassing `BaseDevice` or drops CP1-CP6 (trips the base's composition trap); (4) `introspect()` stops reporting intention -> state -> settings in order; (5) a seal claimed present (isolation='netns') but measured to still hold a route is called anything but BREACHED — a sandbox that reports the shape of a seal while handing out live sockets is the exact defect the tester exists to kill; (6) the trail's chain check reporting only its COMPLAINTS — the three lanes are ELIGIBILITY-nested (a non-record holds no link; an unlinked entry has no hash to compare), and written as a bare list the same emptiness stood for a trail that verified whole, an empty trail, and a trail whose entries had quietly stopped being eligible; (7) an entry appearing GREEN in a lane it was never eligible for — it is ABSENT from that lane's population, and one fault must never multiply into three; (8) ``verify_trail`` growing a second walk instead of reading ``inspect_trail``'s mismatches; (9) any proof in this device typing its own roster of teeth by hand — measured 2026-08-13, two teeth added to test_validation_store.py never ran and the file printed the same green line, so the roster is the module's declaration order and a roster that shrinks trips its own floor.
how_it_learns: Yes — and it is where learning-from-proof concentrates. Every VALIDATION carries falsifier + horizon (Law 3), so each verdict knows how it expires — 'validated on the 17th' can itself go stale and be re-run; a verdict is a best-guess-with-an-expiry, not a permanent stamp. A red is not a failure to suppress but CP2 data (FAIL = Further Advance In Learning), kicked back to design. THE SEAL LEARNS THE SAME WAY: it is measured from inside every run, never assumed, so a misconfigured or silently-downgraded sandbox is CAUGHT rather than trusted; a seal that cannot be confirmed is INDETERMINATE (CP1 made structural — 'I don't know' is a legible verdict, not a hidden green). The component's own horizon: its verdict METHOD is provisional — exit-code+seal today, quorum / review-by-experts for concept pieces later (MAP.md:752); the seal itself will grow from NO-ROUTE to a CHOSEN route (Router) when db/inference domains pull it. The beside-code validation store (validation_store.py) is the evidence trail that turns answered proofs into structure (Law 1) instead of re-derivation — a mind greps validations/ on a hunch rather than re-proving, and because it is git-JSON beside the proof it is durable and shareable by construction (no single un-backed row).
traces_to: Law 8 (a proof a hollow build couldn't pass — the tester IS that gate)
Law 4 (physics over policy — proving + attesting from one hand)
Law 3 (a VALIDATION expires: falsifier + horizon ride along)
Law 5 (intent + code + proofs share this address)
Form v0 #2 (the ordered introspection surface, MAP.md:157)
owner: CC owns the tester's code + proofs and gates writes to them. Akien owns the VALIDATION schema's ratification (MAP.md:569) and the node-class definitions.
proof: proofs/test_tester.py — device-hood + the six, Form v0 #2 order, green->green, red->red (the hollow-tester killer), state reflects runs, exercises the base's armed trap; plus a __main__ dogfood that validates the real base proofs. proofs/test_isolation.py — the network seal: the four seal verdicts measured (incl. the hollow-seal BREACHED case), a LIVE bwrap seal on a capable host (honest INDETERMINATE otherwise), and run_proof folds the seal into the 8 fields with no schema drift. proofs/fixtures/ — a green (exit 0) and a red (exit 1) proof. proofs/test_cli.py — the verb: verdict drift, the hollow green over zero proofs, and the sealing line, each killed by its own case; a red is asserted to carry its evidence in the first run. Green: `cairn test cairn/devices/tester/proofs/` (or `python3 cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_tester.py` bare).

Same day, grew its OTHER half — the kernel-owned network's measured SEAL (cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py) — completing the 'tester + kernel-owned network' spine step's no-route half (MAP.md:888).
